text:
riley: CI started spitting up on edge SDK tests. Both vitest and jest, same suite. getting 'Cannot use import statement outside a module' and some mocks not applying.

dev-bot: nightly-edge-tests · build/edge-tests #512 failed
```
Error: Cannot use import statement outside a module
    at Object.compileFunction (node:vm:360:18)
    at Module._compile (internal/modules/cjs/loader:1092:27)
```

pat: reproducible locally: pnpm -w test --filter @redwood/sdk -- run edge. Looks like conditional exports (dist/runtime.mjs vs dist/runtime.cjs) + test runner resolver differences cause mock identity drift.

kai: vitest inlines deps by default sometimes (vite resolver picks the import entry), jest with transformIgnorePatterns can still hit cjs. result: our fetch mock attaches to a different module object.

mike: quick minimal fix I used in CI: add tests/setup/require-shim.cjs that uses createRequire to load the cjs runtime, and then set jest moduleNameMapper to point @redwood/sdk to that shim; for vitest add deps.inline: ['@redwood/sdk'].

riley: can you paste the shim?

mike: shim contents:
```js
// tests/setup/require-shim.cjs
const { createRequire } = require('module');
const req = createRequire(import.meta.url || __filename);
module.exports = req('../dist/runtime.cjs');
```
And vitest.config.ts snippet:
```ts
export default defineConfig({ test: { deps: { inline: ['@redwood/sdk'] } } })
```
jest.config.js snippet:
```js
module.exports = { transformIgnorePatterns: ['node_modules/(?!@redwood/sdk)'], moduleNameMapper: { '^@redwood/sdk$': '<rootDir>/tests/setup/require-shim.cjs' } }
```

pat: added a small PR with the shim + config tweak. CI passed on linux/mac, windows still flaky but better.

kai: we'll author a short devex doc with recommended patterns (shim + inline deps, or prefer publishing a flat esm-only runtime for edge-only packages).

riley: nice work. closing unless it reappears. :thumbsup:
